cities.name: Shimla
cities.overview: The former summer capital of British India, spread along a ridge at about 2,200 metres. Its colonial buildings, Mall Road and toy-train link to Kalka make it Himachal's best-known hill station.
cities.history: A small hill village until the British took it up in the 19th century and made it the summer capital of British India from 1864. The government moved here from the plains every year until Independence.

cities.name: Manali
cities.overview: A mountain town at the head of the Kullu Valley on the Beas River, the base for Solang Valley, the Atal Tunnel and the road to Lahaul, Spiti and Ladakh.

cities.name: Dharamshala
cities.overview: A town in the Kangra Valley beneath the Dhauladhar range. Upper Dharamshala, McLeod Ganj, is the home of the Dalai Lama and the Tibetan government-in-exile.
cities.history: The headquarters of Kangra district since 1855, and home of the 14th Dalai Lama and the Tibetan government-in-exile since 1960.

cities.name: Bir
cities.overview: A small village in Kangra district known for paragliding, Tibetan monasteries and a relaxed café culture.

cities.name: Kaza
cities.overview: The main town of the Spiti Valley at about 3,800 metres, a cold desert of ancient monasteries and remote villages near the Tibetan border.

cities.name: Kullu
cities.overview: The valley town on the Beas, known for shawls and Dussehra, and the gateway to Parvati Valley.

cities.name: Kasol
cities.overview: A riverside hamlet in Parvati Valley, a base for backpackers and treks.

cities.name: Palampur
cities.overview: A tea town in the Kangra Valley under the Dhauladhar range.

cities.name: Kangra
cities.overview: An old town at the foot of the Dhauladhars, known for its fort and its miniature painting.

cities.name: Dalhousie
cities.overview: A colonial hill station across five hills in Chamba district.

cities.name: Chamba
cities.overview: An old hill capital on the Ravi River, known for its stone temples and embroidered handkerchiefs.

cities.name: Kinnaur
cities.overview: A high apple-growing district on the Sutlej, with Kalpa and Sangla its best-known stops.

cities.name: Mandi
cities.overview: A town of old stone temples on the Beas, and the base for two sacred lakes.

cities.name: Sirmaur
cities.overview: The south-eastern corner of Himachal, home to the state's largest lake.

places.name: The Ridge and Mall Road, Shimla
places.shortDescription: Shimla's open promenade with Christ Church, colonial buildings and views of the Himalayan ranges.
places.description: The Ridge is a wide, traffic-free space at the centre of Shimla, joined to the Mall Road with its shops, cafés and Tudor-style buildings. Christ Church, with its stained-glass windows, stands at one end. From here walk up to the Jakhoo Temple, or down to the Lakkar Bazaar for wooden handicrafts. On clear days the snow peaks are visible to the north.
places.history: Shimla became the summer capital of British India in 1864. Christ Church was completed in 1857 and is the second-oldest church in North India. The Kalka–Shimla Railway was added to the Mountain Railways of India UNESCO listing in 2008.
places.bestTimeNote: March to June for pleasant days; December–January for a chance of snow.

images.alt: The Ridge and Mall Road, Shimla, Shimla

places.name: Hadimba Devi Temple
places.shortDescription: A 16th-century wooden temple with a four-tiered pagoda roof in a cedar forest above Manali.
places.description: The temple is built around a rock where Hadimba, wife of the Pandava prince Bhima in the Mahabharata, is said to have meditated. Its wooden doorway is richly carved with animals, gods and symbols. The surrounding Dhungri forest of tall deodar trees makes it one of the most atmospheric spots in Manali. A spring festival honouring the goddess is held in May.
places.history: Built in 1553 by Maharaja Bahadur Singh of the Kullu kingdom.

location.address: Hadimba Temple Road, Dhungri Van Vihar, Manali, Himachal Pradesh 175131

places.name: Solang Valley
places.shortDescription: Manali's adventure hub for paragliding and zorbing in summer and skiing and snow play in winter.
places.description: Solang Valley, 14 km from Manali, has slopes for short tandem paragliding flights, zorbing and ATV rides in summer, and skiing and snowboarding in winter. A ropeway climbs to Mount Phatru for views of glaciers and peaks. The south portal of the Atal Tunnel, which leads to Lahaul, is a short drive away.
places.bestTimeNote: January to March for snow; May, June and October for paragliding.

entryFee.note: Activities and the ropeway are priced separately; agree rates with registered operators.

timings.hours: Activities usually 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM, weather permitting

location.address: Solang, Burwa, Manali, Kullu district, Himachal Pradesh 175131

places.name: Tsuglagkhang Complex
places.shortDescription: The main temple of McLeod Ganj and the residence of the 14th Dalai Lama.
places.description: The complex includes the Tsuglagkhang temple with statues of the Buddha, Avalokiteshvara and Padmasambhava, the Namgyal Monastery, where monks can be seen debating in the courtyard, and the Tibet Museum, which tells the story of Tibetan exile. Visitors walk the kora, a forested circuit lined with prayer wheels and prayer flags, around the complex.
places.history: Built after the Dalai Lama fled Tibet in 1959 and settled in Dharamshala, which became the seat of the Tibetan government-in-exile.

entryFee.note: The Tibet Museum charges a small fee.

location.address: Temple Road, McLeod Ganj, Dharamshala, Himachal Pradesh 176219

places.name: Bir Billing
places.shortDescription: One of the world's top paragliding sites, with flights from Billing's 2,400-metre take-off down to Bir.
places.description: Tandem pilots launch from the meadow at Billing and glide for 15 to 30 minutes over pine forests, tea gardens and villages before landing at Bir. Experienced pilots fly cross-country for hours along the Dhauladhar range. Back on the ground, Bir has Tibetan monasteries, a colony of Tibetan refugees and laid-back cafés.
places.history: Bir Billing hosted the Paragliding World Cup in 2015.
places.bestTimeNote: March to May and October to November. Flying usually stops during the monsoon (mid-July to mid-September).

entryFee.note: Tandem flights are priced per flight; choose registered pilots with valid licences.

timings.hours: Flights usually from late morning to mid-afternoon

location.address: Bir, Baijnath tehsil, Kangra district, Himachal Pradesh 176077

places.name: Key Monastery
places.shortDescription: A thousand-year-old Buddhist monastery stacked on a hilltop above the Spiti River at about 4,100 metres.
places.description: Key (Kee) Gompa's whitewashed buildings climb a conical hill above the Spiti Valley like a small fortress. Inside are prayer halls, murals, old manuscripts and a community of monks, who often offer visitors butter tea. Nearby are the high villages of Kibber and Langza, among the highest villages connected by road. Give yourself time to adjust to the altitude.
places.history: According to tradition the monastery was founded about a thousand years ago, around the time of the teacher Rinchen Zangpo. It was attacked several times over the centuries, which explains its fortress-like layout.
places.bestTimeNote: May to October. The Manali–Kaza road via Kunzum Pass is usually open from June to October; the Shimla–Kinnaur route stays open longer.

location.address: Key Monastery, Kaza, Lahaul and Spiti district, Himachal Pradesh 172114

places.name: Rashtrapati Niwas
places.shortDescription: The former Viceregal Lodge on Observatory Hill, summer home of the British Viceroys.
places.description: A grey stone Scottish-style mansion with wood-panelled rooms and big lawns. Guided tours take in the rooms where the Partition of India was discussed.
places.history: Formerly the Viceroy's residence. The building now also houses the Indian Institute of Advanced Study.

places.name: Jakhu Temple
places.shortDescription: A Hanuman temple on Shimla's highest peak, 2,455 m, with a giant statue of the god.
places.description: A steep 2.5 km walk or a short ropeway ride from the Ridge. The giant orange Hanuman can be seen from most of the town, and the monkeys here will take your glasses.

places.name: Christ Church, Shimla
places.shortDescription: The second oldest church in north India, a pale yellow landmark on the Ridge.
places.description: Its neo-Gothic tower and stained glass windows make it the most recognisable sight on Shimla's skyline. Services are held in Hindi and English.

places.name: Kufri
places.shortDescription: A small hill resort 12 km from Shimla, known for yak rides, snow and a Himalayan nature park.
places.description: A busy stop on the road out of Shimla, with pony rides up to Mahasu Peak and snow play in winter. The Himalayan Nature Park keeps local wildlife.

places.name: Chail
places.shortDescription: A quiet hill station 44 km from Shimla, with a Maharaja's palace and one of the world's highest cricket grounds.
places.description: Thick cedar forest surrounds this former summer capital of Patiala. The Chail Palace is now a hotel, and the cricket ground is still in use.

places.name: Narkanda
places.shortDescription: A ski and apple town at 2,708 m on the Hindustan-Tibet Road, with Hatu Peak above it.
places.description: Apple orchards and beginner ski slopes in winter, with a forest road up to the Hatu Mata temple at the top of the peak.

places.name: Kalka–Shimla Railway
places.shortDescription: A narrow-gauge UNESCO mountain railway climbing to Shimla through more than a hundred tunnels.
places.description: A slow toy train from the plains at Kalka up to Shimla, over arched bridges and through tunnels. The route is part of the Mountain Railways of India UNESCO listing.
places.history: Opened in 1903 to link the summer capital to the plains.

images.credit: No machine-readable author provided. AHEMSLTD assumed (based on copyright claims)

places.name: Rohtang Pass
places.shortDescription: A high pass 51 km from Manali, linking the Kullu Valley to Lahaul and Spiti.
places.description: Snow lasts here well into summer, and it's the classic day trip from Manali. Vehicle permits are limited, so check the rules in advance.
places.bestTimeNote: The pass is closed by snow for several months each winter, and vehicles need a permit.

places.name: Atal Tunnel
places.shortDescription: A 9.02 km road tunnel under the Pir Panjal, bypassing Rohtang Pass and linking Manali to Keylong.
places.description: It cut hours off the journey to Lahaul and keeps the valley connected through winter. Sissu, on the far side, has become a popular stop with waterfalls and a lake.

places.name: Naggar Castle
places.shortDescription: A medieval stone and timber castle above the Beas, now a heritage hotel near Manali.
places.description: A fine example of the region's layered stone and wood building, looking across the Kullu Valley. The Roerich Art Gallery is a short walk uphill.
places.history: Built by Raja Sidh Singh of Kullu around 1460.

places.name: Manikaran
places.shortDescription: A Sikh and Hindu pilgrim town in Parvati Valley, known for boiling hot springs.
places.description: A big gurdwara and several temples crowd the riverbank, and the langar's rice is cooked in the hot spring water. It's 4 km from Kasol.

places.name: Great Himalayan National Park
places.shortDescription: A UNESCO World Heritage park in Kullu, with high forests and rare pheasants, explored only on foot.
places.description: No roads go in, so visitors trek through forests and alpine meadows from Sainj and Tirthan valleys. Western tragopan, musk deer and snow leopards live here.
places.history: Established in 1984, and added to the UNESCO World Heritage list in 2014.

places.name: Bijli Mahadev
places.shortDescription: A hilltop Shiva temple at 2,460 m, where lightning is said to strike the lingam regularly.
places.description: A hike of a couple of hours through forest leads to a wooden temple on a ridge, with views over the Kullu and Parvati valleys.

places.name: Triund
places.shortDescription: The classic Dhauladhar day hike, a grassy ridge at about 2,850 m above McLeod Ganj.
places.description: A steady climb through oak and rhododendron ends on a meadow right below the snow wall of the Dhauladhars. Camping out for the sunrise is popular.

places.name: McLeod Ganj
places.shortDescription: Little Lhasa: the Tibetan hill suburb of Dharamshala, home of the Tibetan government-in-exile.
places.description: Prayer wheels, momo stalls and monks fill the lanes. It's an easy base for short walks to Bhagsu Falls and the Dharamkot cafes.

places.name: Kangra Fort
places.shortDescription: A vast old fort between two rivers, also known as Nagarkot, seat of the Katoch rulers.
places.description: Long walls on a rock above the Banganga and Patal Ganga rivers. Though much was wrecked by the 1905 earthquake, the gates and temples remain.
places.history: Mahmud of Ghazni and later Mughal rulers all fought over this rich stronghold.

places.name: Masrur Temples
places.shortDescription: An early 8th-century group of rock-cut temples in the Kangra Valley, facing a sacred pool.
places.description: Carved out of one sandstone ridge, in a style rare this far north. The reflection of the temples in the tank makes it worth the drive.

places.name: Jwala Ji Temple
places.shortDescription: A goddess temple in Kangra district where eternal flames burn from the rock.
places.description: There's no idol: the deity is worshipped as natural flames coming out of the rock. It's one of the most-visited temples in Himachal.

places.name: Baijnath Temple
places.shortDescription: A Nagara-style Shiva temple built in 1204 by two merchants, in the Kangra Valley.
places.description: A fine stone temple with carved panels and long inscriptions, set against the Dhauladhars. It's still in active worship.
places.history: Built in 1204 AD by two local merchants, Ahuka and Manyuka.

places.name: Khajjiar
places.shortDescription: A saucer-shaped meadow ringed with deodar forest, 24 km from Dalhousie.
places.description: Often sold as a mini Switzerland, this green bowl has a small lake in the middle and a gold-domed Naga temple. Pony rides and zorbing crowd it in season.

places.name: Lakshmi Narayan Temples, Chamba
places.shortDescription: A group of stone Shikhara temples at the heart of Chamba, on the bank of the Ravi.
places.description: Six tall temples stand together in a courtyard in the old town, with wooden umbrellas on top. Chamba's Bhuri Singh Museum and Minjar Fair are nearby attractions.

places.name: Pin Valley National Park
places.shortDescription: A cold-desert park in Spiti, known for snow leopards, ibex and the villages around Mud.
places.description: Bare mountains in pink and grey, with the Pin River running through them. The winter snow leopard expeditions are famous among wildlife photographers.

places.name: Chandra Taal
places.shortDescription: The Moon Lake, a high blue lake in Lahaul near the source of the Chandra River.
places.description: A crescent of blue water at 4,300 m, reached by a rough track off the Kunzum road. Camping is allowed only some way from the shore.
places.bestTimeNote: The road opens only from about June to October, once the snow clears.

places.name: Kunzum Pass
places.shortDescription: The high pass between Lahaul and Spiti, with a small temple to Kunzum Mata at the top.
places.description: A wide, windy saddle at about 4,590 m on the road to Kaza, with views of Bara Shigri glacier. Drivers traditionally stop and circle the temple.

places.name: Dhankar Monastery
places.shortDescription: A gompa perched on a crumbling spur at 3,894 m, above the Spiti and Pin rivers.
places.description: One of the world's most spectacularly placed monasteries, and among those on the list of most endangered sites. A short hike goes up to the high Dhankar Lake.

places.name: Tabo Monastery
places.shortDescription: A 996 CE monastery in Spiti, with some of the finest early Buddhist murals in the Himalayas.
places.description: From outside it looks like plain mud-brick halls. Inside, thousand-year-old murals and clay sculptures fill the dim rooms, so bring a torch.
places.history: Founded in 996 CE by the translator Rinchen Zangpo.

places.name: Kalpa
places.shortDescription: A village above Reckong Peo, with views straight across to the Kinner Kailash range.
places.description: Apple orchards and old wooden temples look out on one of the most dramatic mountain views in Himachal, especially at sunrise.

images.credit: Carlos Adampol Galindo from DF, México

places.name: Sangla Valley
places.shortDescription: The Baspa Valley in Kinnaur, a high green valley of orchards, wooden villages and snow peaks.
places.description: One of Himachal's prettiest valleys, with apple orchards and the old Kamru Fort. The road runs along the Baspa toward Chitkul.

places.name: Chitkul
places.shortDescription: The last inhabited village on the old Indo-Tibet road in Kinnaur, on the Baspa River.
places.description: Slate roofs, wooden houses and a meadow by the river, close to the Tibet border. Villagers move lower down for the snowy winter.

places.name: Prashar Lake
places.shortDescription: A high lake at 2,730 m with a floating island and a three-storied pagoda temple.
places.description: A small sacred lake in a grassy bowl, with a circular island that's said to move about the water. There's a short walk from the road, which makes for a great day trip.

places.name: Rewalsar Lake
places.shortDescription: Tso Pema, a lake at 1,360 m sacred to Buddhists, Hindus and Sikhs, 22.5 km from Mandi.
places.description: A small lake surrounded by a monastery, a gurdwara and temples. A giant statue of Padmasambhava, the Buddhist saint, looks down from the hill.

places.name: Renuka Lake
places.shortDescription: The largest natural lake in Himachal Pradesh, in Sirmaur, named after the goddess Renuka.
places.description: A long green lake shaped like a sleeping woman, with boats and a small wildlife park nearby. A fair is held here each November.
